page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The CPU includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

This instance is equipped with 402 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed local disk access directly attached to the host. In terms of performance, the instance exhibits average single-core capabilities, as demonstrated by its stress-ng single-core score of 1617.89 and Geekbench single-core score of 1714.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3323.04 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3812.0. Memory bandwidth is also a limiting factor, with uncached large-block read and write speeds measuring 29.2 GB/sec and 22.26 GB/sec respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-standard-4-lssd offers a balanced resource profile for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation and high-speed local storage without the overhead of larger instance sizes. The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage makes it a viable option for applications requiring low-latency scratch space. However, the tradeoff lies in its constrained multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth, which may bottleneck highly parallel or memory-intensive tasks.

This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, light database operations, static web serving, and basic text processing tasks. It can also handle lightweight single-threaded applications and small-scale software compilation where the local SSD can be leveraged for fast file access.
